fix: Hoist the set out of the per-event closure so its table is reused: before `selected.into_iter()` add `let mut visited = HashSet::new();`, then replace the in-closure `let mut visited = HashSet::new();` with `visited.clear();` at the start of the closure body. The closure becomes FnMut, which `map` accepts. Cycle detection and depth results are unchanged.

Borrow the options instead of cloning them: make `EditorKind` generic over a lifetime (`pub enum EditorKind<'a>`), change `Segmented`, `Menu` and `AlignmentGrid` to hold `&'a [String]`, and make `pub fn editor_kind(property: &DebugProperty) -> EditorKind<'_>` return `EditorKind::AlignmentGrid(&property.options)`, `EditorKind::Segmented(&property.options)` and `EditorKind::Menu(&property.options)`. Update the call sites that match on these variants so they accept a slice.

Avoid allocating the key on every call (`entry` needs an owned String, so `to_owned()` runs even when the key is present). Use: `if !self.values.contains_key(key) { self.values.insert(key.to_owned(), current.clone()); }`. The key is allocated and the value cloned only when a property is first recorded.

Same pattern as OriginalValues::record: allocate the key only when the slot is missing. Use: `if !self.slots.contains_key(key) { self.slots.insert(key.to_owned(), Slot::default()); }` followed by `let slot = self.slots.get_mut(key).expect("slot inserted above");`. Each edit offer then no longer allocates a String for an existing property.
